name: Firebase installation ID
plain: A random per-install ID created by the Firebase SDK.
meaning: Fresh per app install; many SDKs use it as a first-party ID and link it to other IDs server-side.

android.note: 22-character ID, valid until app data is cleared or the app is uninstalled; deleted if unused for 270 days

limits.headline: Can recognize this one install of the app with a random ID, until it is removed
limits.user_action: Nothing. The ID is created the first time the app connects to the internet
can: Tell one install of the app apart from another with a 22 character random ID
Link usage, crashes and messages to that same install over time
Keep the same ID until you clear the app's data or uninstall it
cannot: Follow you to other apps or other phones; the ID belongs to this install only
Survive an uninstall or Clear data; a new ID is made afterward
Stay alive forever on Android if the app goes unused; it is deleted after 270 days

story.what_it_is: A random ID made for each app install by Google's Firebase toolkit.

marketing.name: Firebase installations
marketing.pitch: Developer pitch: a stable, unique ID for each install of your app, used by Firebase services like messaging and analytics.

story.for_you: You never see it. It quietly lets the app and Google's tools tell your phone apart from every other install, and it resets if you delete and reinstall the app.
story.for_makers: Makers get a free, always available ID to count users, send push notifications and run tests. It lets crash reports, experiments and notifications line up for one install without asking for any permission.

use_cases.example: A game studio uses the install ID to give one phone the same A/B test version of the tutorial every time it opens the game.
A chat app uses the ID as the address for push notifications, so a message reaches the right phone.
A product team counts daily active installs and links crash reports to one install without asking you to sign in.
An ad network links an install to a later in-app purchase so it can tell which campaign paid off.
A store app shows you the same test version of its checkout page on each visit, so results stay clean.
A bank sees ten new accounts opened from one install ID and flags a possible fraud ring.

risks: Can be joined to other IDs on a server
story.android_note: Available to any app that includes Firebase, with no prompt.
story.ios_note: Works the same way on iPhone, created fresh for each install of the app.
